description: Raise the fused megakernel's occupancy from 1 to 2 CTAs/SM -- the single highest-EV lever left, grounded in two prior briefs' root-cause. The megakernel (mega_eigh n<=200, mega_eigh_med 200<n<=448) is the HOT kernel on 5 benchmark shapes (1,2 direct + 3,8,12 as the low-rank inner solve). brief-13 proved it is BARRIER-BOUND: at 1 CTA/SM (50% occ) each __syncthreads stalls all warps with no second resident block to hide behind, so barrier-count cuts recovered only ~1%; the 1-CTA/SM cap is set by BOTH the 127KB packed-FP16 SMEM AND 64 regs/thread. brief-14 proved launch_bounds(nt,2) removes the register cap (regs->2 CTAs/SM). The ONLY remaining blocker is SMEM: halve the packed lower-triangle from FP16 (~127KB) to FP8 / B200-native block-scaled MXFP8 (~64KB) so 2 CTAs fit -> occupancy doubles -> the barrier stalls are hidden -> up to ~2x across all 5 megakernel shapes. CRITICAL: FP8 for STORAGE only, dequantize to FP16/FP32 for the reduction arithmetic (brief-3's FP8-COMPUTE reduction was 100% fallback; storage+dequant is different). Add launch_bounds(nt,2). Preserve accuracy via per-row/block scaling (microscaling); explore a hybrid FP16-near-diagonal-band + FP8-far layout if flat FP8 is too coarse. All residual-gated so any FP8 quantization error falls to cuSOLVER (bounded downside, no regression). Forks best 12251fe. -O2 not -O3; no 'stream' substring; do not regress shapes 1/2/3/8/12.

FP8 e4m3 storage (per-row scaled) of the packed lower triangle in mega_eigh_med_k + __launch_bounds__(1024,2), -O2. NCU CONFIRMS THE THESIS: occupancy 50%->92.9% (Block Limit Registers 1->2 via launch_bounds; Block Limit SharedMem 1->2 via FP8 shrink to 108.5KB dynamic; regs/thread 48->32). BUT flat FP8's 3-bit mantissa is too coarse for the sequential Householder rank-2 updates -> heavy cuSOLVER fallback (validation orth residuals ~0.5 >> internal gate 0.006) -> benchmark REGRESSED to 58637us vs parent 41378. Occupancy win real but wasted by fallback.

HYBRID FP16-near-band + FP8-far packed storage; auto-pick largest BAND fitting 2-CTA cap (n=352 BAND~152=32% FP8; n=384 BAND~88=59% FP8). Validated PASS. Benchmark geomean 65919us -- measured under HEAVY concurrent fleet load (untouched cuSOLVER shape5 n2048 inflated 186099->221444, ~19%), so absolute numbers are contention-noisy. Relative signal: shape2 n352 improved vs t1 (39535->22922) confirming band-FP16 cuts fallback where FP16 coverage is high; k=384 shapes (8,12) still fallback-dominated + hybrid per-element index ALU adds symv cost. Both FP8 variants regress vs parent 41378.

Precomputed per-row band/far offset tables (bo,fo in SMEM) to remove per-element index ALU from the symv. BUT this commit (like t2) FAILED TO COMPILE -- the hybrid AGET used (float)Hb[__half] which is rejected under torch's __CUDA_NO_HALF_CONVERSIONS__; _mega_get's try/except swallowed it -> _mega_failed=True -> all megakernel paths silently ran torch.linalg.eigh. build.sh only imports (no load_inline) so reported BUILD_OK. Benchmark 48582us was therefore PURE cuSOLVER for the megakernel shapes (which usefully measures the megakernel's geomean worth: ~15%, 41378 with vs 48582 without). NOT a valid FP8 measurement.

FIXED the __half2float compile bug -> hybrid FP8 megakernel now ACTUALLY COMPILES+RUNS (verified MODULE:OK). Clean 3x benchmark 60184/60407/60122us (stable) = +45% vs parent 41378. DECISIVE probe: 100% fallback on ALL 5 megakernel shapes -- direct n352 orth=134 (gate 3e-3), lr k352 orth=2.3e4, lr k384 orth=1.85e5/27.7, all >> gate. FP8 far-off-diagonal corrupts the symv -> non-orthonormal eigenvectors (eigenvalues OK from FP16-band diagonal, but orthogonality fatally broken). AND raw megakernel 23807us > cuSOLVER 20445us at n352 b40 (2 CTAs slower even ignoring fallback; ncu: same b640 k352 kernel 52.14ms@1CTA -> 62.85ms@2CTA). Occupancy DID double (50->93%, ncu) but the kernel is ALU-bound+lockstep-barrier so 2 resident CTAs contend rather than overlap. Two independent failure modes (slower kernel + 100% orth fallback) both -> regression.

BANK non-regressing state per coordinator: FP8-occupancy lever REFUTED, restore proven packed-FP16 mega_eigh_med_k as the active med path (route the losing FP8 path nowhere), keep the -O2 brief mandate. Validated PASS; 3x benchmark 45701/42296/42247us = parent-level (stable ~42.2us; the 41378 parent used -O3 --use_fast_math, this honors the -O2 mandate). FP8 finding documented inline + full FP8 source preserved in trials 1-4 history+profiles. SUMMARY of the refutation: occupancy DID double 50%->92.9% (ncu; FP8 shrink 127->108KB SMEM + launch_bounds(1024,2) both->Block Limit 2) but (a) 2 CTAs made the ALU-bound/lockstep-barrier kernel SLOWER not faster -- same b640 k352 kernel 52.14ms@1CTA -> 62.85ms flat-FP8 / 77.87ms hybrid @2CTA (barriers wait on 64 warps, CTAs contend for ALU), and (b) FP8's 3-bit mantissa broke eigenvector orthogonality -> 100% cuSOLVER fallback on ALL 5 shapes (orth 134..1.85e5 vs gate ~3e-3..1e-2; even n=352 hybrid at 68% FP16). The FP16 coverage to pass the orth gate exceeds the 2-CTA SMEM budget -> fundamental tension. Net +45% regression when active.

FP8-storage occupancy lever: MECHANISM CONFIRMED, NET REGRESSION, banked non-regressing. 5 trials on mega_eigh_med_k.

THESIS PROVEN (ncu, trial 1, b640 k352): FP8 e4m3 packed lower triangle (1B) + __launch_bounds__(1024,2) dropped dynamic SMEM 127->108.5KB and regs 48->32, so Block Limit SharedMem AND Registers BOTH went 1->2, Theoretical Occupancy 50->100%, Achieved 50->92.9%. Exactly what brief-13/14 predicted -- 2 CTAs/SM is reachable.

BUT +45% REGRESSION (41378->60184us stable, trial 4), for TWO independent MEASURED reasons:
(a) 2 CTAs make the kernel SLOWER, not faster. mega_eigh_med_k is ALU-bound (~24% ALU util, unchanged at 2 CTAs) and barrier-heavy; two resident CTAs run identical code in near-lockstep so they CONTEND for the same ALU pipes and each __syncthreads now waits on 64 warps instead of 32 -> Warp Cycles/Issued Inst 17.7->28.6, LENGTHENING barrier stalls rather than hiding them. Same b640 k352 kernel duration: 52.14ms@1CTA -> 62.85ms(flat FP8)/77.87ms(hybrid)@2CTA. At small batch (b40 shape2) it is doubly bad -- 40 blocks pack onto 20 SMs vs spreading across 40.
(b) FP8's 3-bit mantissa is FATAL for eigenvector orthogonality -> 100% cuSOLVER fallback on ALL 5 shapes (probe: orth residual 134..1.85e5 vs gate ~3e-3..1e-2). Eigenvalues survive (FP16-band diagonal) but far-off-diagonal FP8 entries corrupt symv p=A@v -> reflectors -> non-orthonormal Q. HYBRID FP16-near-band + FP8-far tried (n=352 gets 68% FP16, orth STILL 134); the FP16 coverage needed to pass the orth gate (~all) exceeds the SMEM budget 2 CTAs require -- a fundamental tension. Even zero-fallback would not win: raw megakernel 23807us already > cuSOLVER 20445us at n352 b40.

GOTCHA FOUND+FIXED: trials 2&3 (hybrid) SILENTLY compiled-failed -- (float)__half is rejected under torch's __CUDA_NO_HALF_CONVERSIONS__ and _mega_get()'s try/except swallowed it -> _mega_failed -> all megakernel paths ran pure cuSOLVER (build.sh only imports, no load_inline, so it reported BUILD_OK). Fixed with __half2float (t4). Useful side-measurement: pure-cuSOLVER-for-megakernel-shapes = 48582us, so the megakernel is worth ~15% of the geomean (41378 with vs 48582 without).

BANKED (t5, HEAD 408fa28b): restored the proven packed-FP16 mega_eigh_med_k as the active path (FP8 routed nowhere -- it wins nowhere), kept the -O2 mandate. Validated PASS, 3x bench 45701/42296/42247us = parent-level (~42.2us; the 41378 parent used -O3/fast-math, this honors -O2). nsys confirms 0 fallback kernels. FP8 source fully preserved in git history t1-4 + profiles. Non-regressing.

OPEN directions (manager's call -- all must still clear the orthogonality-gate wall, the dominant blocker):
1. ISOLATE cause (a): an FP16 + __launch_bounds__(1024,2) 1-CTA control (32 regs, still SMEM-capped to 1 CTA) vs the parent (48 regs, 1 CTA) would tell whether the register clamp itself slows the kernel or it is purely 2-CTA contention. If the clamp is free, a NON-FP8 occupancy path (e.g. shrink SMEM by a smarter layout, or a naturally-<=32-reg kernel refactor) might still get 2 CTAs -- but only helps if cause (a) is contention, which the duration data suggests is real regardless.
2. Batch-gated launch: use 2 CTAs/SM only when batch >> 148 SMs (large-batch low-rank inners), 1 CTA/SM for small direct batches (shape2 b40). Doesn't fix (a) at b640 or (b).
3. The n<=200 mega_eigh_k kernel (shape 1) was NOT touched -- it has the same 1-CTA/barrier structure and could be probed, but the same two walls apply.
4. Precision: FP8x2 residual (~FP16 accuracy) costs 2B = no SMEM saving; MXFP8/block-scaling does not add mantissa bits so does not fix orthogonality. No FP8 variant appears able to both pass the orth gate AND keep 2 CTAs -- this is the core finding.

Bottom line: the FP8-occupancy idea is a clean, well-measured REFUTATION for this kernel (occupancy doubles but does not pay off), banked non-regressing. Recommend redirecting workers off FP8-storage-for-occupancy toward barrier/ALU-work reduction or the low-rank outer-GEMM precision (brief-16 line, now global best 40228).
